name: Into Another
label: Revelation
lede: A Youth of Today singer, a Bold drummer and a thrash bassist put a Wurlitzer into hard rock, and the hardcore kids stagedived anyway, until a major label shipped the album with somebody else's music on the disc.

eras.title: Out of the box on the Lower East Side
eras.text: Richie Birkenhead and Drew Thomas came out of youth crew hardcore and wanted none of its rules. They found a guitarist who could really play and a bassist from a thrash band, then made something nobody at the matinee had asked for.

q: We were unbelievably surprised that we were embraced to the degree that we were.
years.h: Birkenhead and Thomas recruit a thrash bassist and a guitarist
years.p: Richie Birkenhead ([[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]], [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]]) and Drew Thomas ([[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], [[Crippled Youth|ad695a64-ac47-4320-a0c2-3aa7a4c5abc4]]) bring in guitarist Peter Moses and bassist [[Tony Bono|7ca7aa95-78a3-4330-9fac-390d6dfc6646]], late of the thrash band Whiplash. The plan is to belong to no genre at all.
years.xp:
Birkenhead says he and Thomas joked about alienating people, and wanted to be free of having to conform to anything. What they got instead was a scene that followed them. He told Anti-Matter, "We were unbelievably surprised that we were embraced to the degree that we were."

Revelation's own bio pins the sound down: one foot in the New York hardcore family, the other fishing through classic rock.

years.h: A debut on Revelation that sounds like neither founder's old band
years.p: Into Another comes out on the label behind Youth of Today and Bold, the old bands of Birkenhead and Thomas.

eras.title: The buzz band
eras.text: The records got stranger and the crowds got bigger. By Ignaurus, Into Another was named in the same breath as Quicksand and Orange 9mm, New York hardcore alumni the rock world had started watching.

years.p: The EP lands on Revelation with Birkenhead, Moses, Bono and Thomas still intact.

years.h: Ignaurus turns a hardcore band into a buzz band
years.p: Hard rock, alt-rock, grunge and post-hardcore on one record that somehow holds together. On the West Coast, the Sloth Crew kids are stagediving to it.

eras.title: The Hollywood mistake
eras.text: The major-label deal was supposed to be the payoff, with a producer who had made Pearl Jam's Ten and a single on rock radio. It turned into a case study in how a label can sink a band, and it ended Into Another.

years.h: Herbivore and Poison Fingers close out the Revelation years
years.p: The last two Revelation releases of the original run.
The Disney-owned label pairs the band with [[Rick Parashar|ad1ea089-1b0a-454c-bb29-c5477d612137]], who produced Pearl Jam's Ten.
Cut at London Bridge Studios in Seattle, then Shelter Island and Sorcerer Sound in New York. Birkenhead plays Wurlitzer, Thomas adds congas, and Victor Axelrod sits in on Hammond B3.
years.xp: Parashar produced. Birkenhead has called him the most down to earth, unpretentious guy in the world.

years.big: The single charted. The album wasn't in stores.
years.h: Some copies of Seemless ship with another band's music on the disc
years.p: Birkenhead's account: the wrong CD went out in some regions, and the Mutate Me video aired with the volume turned down.
years.xp:
Birkenhead told Anti-Matter that outside North America the label pressed another band's music onto the disc. T.A.I.L. was on rock radio while CDs were hard to find. He blames terrible distribution and promotion and says Hollywood breached the contract more than once.

When the band talked about suing, he says the label told them it would keep them in it until they were old and gray. Into Another took what he calls a tiny fraction of what they were owed. A key member clause also kept him from performing or recording for two years.

years.h: T.A.I.L. gets to No. 39 on rock radio
years.p: Noah Bogen directs the video for the Seemless single. It peaks at No. 39 on Billboard's Mainstream Rock Tracks.

years.h: Soul Control never comes out, and the band breaks up
years.p: The final album, leaning electronica, is recorded for Hollywood and shelved. Worn down by internal conflict and the label, Into Another splits the same year.

eras.title: After Tony Bono
eras.text: Into Another had been over for years, but losing bassist Tony Bono closed a door everyone had assumed would stay open a crack.

years.big: He was the backbone and the glue.
q: He was the backbone and the glue; he held it all together.
years.p: Blabbermouth reports the bassist died overnight after an apparent heart attack, while playing in the hard rock trio FR8. Birkenhead was in Los Angeles when he heard.
years.xp: Birkenhead drove across the country for the funeral. He described Bono to Anti-Matter as strangely pure, with bass playing that was fertile ground for his lyrics. He took that loss harder than any other he can remember, and for a decade it made a reunion feel impossible.

eras.title: Two younger players bring them back
eras.text: It took Revelation's anniversary, and two musicians who grew up on the records, to get Peter Moses out of retirement upstate. The reunion stuck, and eventually it made new music.

years.cap: Richie Birkenhead, Peter Moses and Drew Thomas at Revelation 25, The Glasshouse, Pomona, June 2012
years.h: Into Another plays Revelation 25 in Pomona
years.p: Birkenhead, Moses and Thomas come back with [[Brian Balchack|62436915-6d04-4893-a4c4-e6b48d8a4dba]] and Reid Black for the label's 25th anniversary shows at The Glasshouse in California.

years.cap: Birkenhead and a guitarist at Revelation 25, The Glasshouse, Pomona, 2012
years.h: Omens is the first new music in nearly two decades
years.p: The EP, on Ghost Ship, comes from the reunited five-piece.

eras.title: Seemless, found
eras.text: The album Hollywood buried finally turned up where people listen now.

years.p: Into Another's 1995 Hollywood Records album lands on the major streaming services.
years.xp: The 2024 reissue adds two bonus tracks, Anne Dreud's Last Entry and Allthewayrider. For years Birkenhead has said Hollywood deliberately shelved and deleted the album from catalogs, keeping it off iTunes.
